messages:
ashley_support: FYI customer on private deployment seeing intermittent TLS handshake timeouts to our inference endpoint.  Sample error from their app: "TLS handshake timeout after ClientHello" and occasional 502/503 spikes. customer reports 10-30% of requests failing during bursts.
chris_customer: Repro window: 2026-03-16T16:02-16:10 UTC. Private VPC, behind NAT GW. SG outbound only allows TCP 443 to 0.0.0.0/0, inbound only from our controlplane IPs. NACL on subnet: ALLOW 443 both, DENY ephemeral 1024-65535 (team applied hardening last week).
jonah_infra: ok that NACL line stands out. If the NACL blocks ephemeral source ports return traffic will be dropped. Can you capture a short tcpdump from the customer side (or ask them) while hitting the endpoint? e.g.:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host <inference-ip> and port 443 -w /tmp/inf.pcap
```
and also run conntrack check: `sudo conntrack -L | grep <client-ip>`
chris_customer: ran tcpdump for 60s, pasted short summary: many SYNs from client -> server, server SYN,ACK seen then client ACK, then soon after we see RST from NAT gateway IP back to client. Also lots of "UNREPLIED" conntrack entries.
deepa_eng: RST from the NAT/NACL hop strongly suggests return packets are being dropped or rewritten. Two quick repro checks:
1) `openssl s_client -connect <inference-host>:443 -servername <inference-host>` - see if handshake completes and which side resets.
2) `curl -v --resolve <inference-host>:443:<inference-ip> https://<inference-host>/health` to force SNI+connect.
Also, temporarily allow ephemeral ports on both NACL and SG outbound (eg TCP 1024-65535) and test again. NACLs are stateless so you need explicit allow for ephemeral return ports.
chris_customer: ran `openssl s_client` — output shows ClientHello sent, server Certificate, then after first application data we saw `read:errno=104` and a TCP RST in pcap. conntrack shows many `UNREPLIED` and a cluster of `ASSURED` then immediate teardown. traceroute -T -p 443 shows last hop is nat-gw, then no further.
jonah_infra: sounds like the NACL deny is the root cause (stateless drop of return ephemeral ports). Quick mitigation steps we recommend to customer:
- Add NACL rules to ALLOW TCP ephemeral 1024-65535 both directions for that subnet (rule num low enough to evaluate before DENY).
- Also add SG outbound rule to allow ephemeral ports if they have a restrictive outbound SG.
- If using NAT GW, monitor SNAT port exhaustion: `aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --metric-name ActiveConnections ...` or enable VPC flow logs to watch resets.
Commands I usually share: `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc-id>` to inspect, and `sudo conntrack -L | grep <server-ip>` to correlate on host.
ops-bot: @chris_customer created internal ticket INF-SUP-2026-872 for follow-up and CCed infra oncall.
ashley_support: @chris_customer please apply ephemeral allow in a maintenance window and report back. We'll hold until you confirm. :eyes:
chris_customer: rolled NACL change (allowed 1024-65535 TCP both). Immediate smoke test: curl health 1000 reqs, no TLS timeouts, error rate dropped from ~18%->0.7%. Keeping watch for 30m. :thumbsup:
ashley_support: great, marking as resolved pending 30m stable. thanks team!
